circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, hosting the season-concluding Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Formula One venue established in the Middle East, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb. It hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with various supporting racing series, holding an FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit in Spielberg, Austria, originally operated as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually from 1970 through 1987. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, the venue was rebranded as the A1-Ring and returned to the Formula One calendar, hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street circuit in Azerbaijan built along Baku Boulevard, measuring 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One racing. The venue first hosted a Grand Prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the maiden Formula One race staged in the Middle East that same year. The venue, which holds a Grade 1 FIA license and features multiple track configurations, has accommodated various motorsport categories including GP2, endurance racing, and briefly Australian touring cars from 2006 to 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One machinery. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located near the Walloon town of Spa in Belgium, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a Formula One fixture since 1950, when it featured in the championship's inaugural season. The venue has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international motorsport series including sports car racing championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019 before the event's return in 2024. The circuit has expanded its racing calendar to include additional international competitions alongside its primary role as a grand prix host.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English racing venue has been the primary home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, having hosted the championship's inaugural race in 1950. The track alternated with two other circuits during the mid-20th century before becoming the permanent British Grand Prix location, and continues to serve as a venue for multiple motorsport series including MotoGP.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located in Mogyoród near Budapest, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted Formula One's inaugural race behind the Iron Curtain in 1986, selected when F1 leadership sought a competitive venue in Eastern Europe. Built in just eight months, faster than any contemporary Formula One track, the facility opened with its inaugural Grand Prix dedicated to János Drapál, a pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racer.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located north of Milan near Monza, this 5. 793 km Italian circuit opened in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The Italian Grand Prix has called Monza home since 1949, making it one of only four tracks to appear continuously on the Formula One calendar, and its configuration of extended straights and high-speed bends has earned it the nickname "the Temple of Speed.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km figure-eight track situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, and managed by Honda Mobilityland. With a capacity of 155,000 spectators, it stands as one of motorsport's most prestigious venues, hosting rounds of the Formula One World Championship and the Japanese Super Formula series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada near Las Vegas, utilizing roads along the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding area. The track passes by iconic casino and hotel complexes such as Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as well as the MSG Sphere venue, incorporating the city's most recognizable attractions into its layout.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City is named after two racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both perished in racing accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. Formula One returned to this venue in 2015 after a 23-year absence, with the modern iteration hosting the Mexican Grand Prix on a revised track configuration, now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed specifically for Formula One by Apex Circuit Design, it joined the championship calendar in 2022 and primarily hosts the Miami Grand Prix, though Formula E has adopted a modified version of the track beginning in 2025-26.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street circuit situated within Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, weaving around Monaco's harbour. Though officially named after Monaco itself, the track is widely known by the Monte Carlo designation due to its predominant location in that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after its Formula One return in 2021, with the partnership concluding in 2026. The venue earned its nickname "The Roller coaster in the Dunes" from its distinctive combination of steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz alongside dramatic elevation shifts through the sandy landscape, creating a uniquely demanding racing experience.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit is situated in the Lusail area north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a principal straight measuring 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: This São Paulo venue, officially named after late driver José Carlos Pace, spans 4. 309 kilometers and has hosted racing since its 1940 opening. The counterclockwise circuit became a Formula One fixture and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Pace following his fatal aviation accident eight years earlier, with the driver's remains relocated there in 2024.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, which has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since 2021. The track also serves as the home for international motorsport events including Formula E competitions starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, utilizing public roads that encircle the bay and connect the city center with the Kallang area.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the 4. 657 km circuit features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple aspects of vehicle performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major motorsport events including NASCAR, MotoGP, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race. The venue has previously accommodated various other racing series ranging from IndyCar to rallycross and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a Thai-British driver, currently races for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish racing driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships in 2005 and 2006 with Renault alongside 32 race victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both F1 and sportscar world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli has been competing in Formula One with Mercedes since his 2025 debut, during which he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian racing driver, currently competes in Formula One representing Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, having previously achieved two runner-up championship finishes during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Across his 13-season career, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine, bringing his talent to the grid.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his motorsport career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver with French and Algerian heritage representing France, currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has secured seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. The 106-time race winner also holds multiple records including most pole positions and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing considerable experience from his extensive career in the sport. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved a notable victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche in endurance racing.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently races for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver competes for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured nine race victories over his nine-season tenure in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while racing for the Maranello team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he competes as a factory driver for BMW in the World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also taking on a part-time role in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver who claimed the 2025 world championship while racing for McLaren. The competitor has secured 13 Grand Prix victories during his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The versatile competitor achieved a significant career milestone by claiming victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican motorsport competitor, currently races in Formula One for Cadillac. The driver achieved runner-up status in the 2023 championship standings while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian motorsport competitor, currently drives for McLaren in Formula One, where he has accumulated nine race victories throughout his four-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for fourteen years between 2011 and 2024, claiming eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight race victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously raced in the IMSA SportsCar Championship's LMP2 division.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing under his commonly used racing name rather than his full surname Strulovitch.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, currently holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing as a full-time Formula One competitor throughout 2021 to 2025, transitioning to a support role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing, securing four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, Verstappen has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a Formula One driver and currently holds a reserve position with Cadillac. The racing driver competed in the championship across three seasons from 2022 through 2024, establishing himself as the sole Chinese competitor to have participated in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed under the Alpine Racing name since 2021, when Renault rebranded its long-standing works operation to highlight the Alpine sports car division. Operating with various title sponsors including BWT, the squad maintained factory backing from Renault throughout its tenure until the manufacturer's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has returned to Formula One competition under the current entity AMR GP Limited, operating as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, holds the distinction of being Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team. Competing continuously since the championship's inaugural 1950 season, the squad is colloquially known as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, and remains unmatched in terms of historical longevity and competitive achievement within the sport.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: The American-licensed outfit established by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas began competing in Formula One in 2016, operating as an independent entry on the grid. Led by team principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, the squad has operated continuously since its inaugural campaign.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering and racing firm operated as an independent Formula One constructor from 1993 until 2025, becoming the fourth-longest competing team by race entries. Originally established in 1970 for sports car manufacturing, the squad achieved endurance racing success including a 1989 Le Mans victory before transitioning to single-seater competition. Audi acquired the organization in 2024 to serve as the technical and operational foundation for its factory Formula One program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, with full ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 in both manufacturing and team ownership capacities. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas operation, based in Brackley and licensed under German colours, became a tri-owned entity in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing operations are traditionally known by the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team within the Red Bull F1 structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls, based in Faenza, is an Italian Formula One constructor that joined the grid in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second team alongside Red Bull Racing. The outfit maintains operational facilities in both Italy and Milton Keynes, functioning as a sister team within the Red Bull motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence despite being based in England, was established in 2005 and became one of two Formula One operations owned by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, after which Laurent Mekies took over as team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian sponsorship banner.
